new_findings.basin: validate_v6_assurance.py `_tracked_set` (:156-168) trusts `git -C root rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` without confirming root is that repo's toplevel: a legitimate, byte-exact NON-git copy of the tree (e.g. an extracted tarball) placed anywhere inside an unrelated git repo answers is-inside-work-tree=true for the FOREIGN repo, `git ls-files` then returns the foreign (typically empty/unrelated) tracked set, and the new INVENTORY_UNTRACKED guard false-alarms on every inventoried path despite all digests verifying
new_findings.evidence: Seat-executed probe (own scratch dir, source untouched): outer `git init` repo with one unrelated tracked file; inner/scripts/tool.py copied in, never added; module loaded from the C+1 validator; `_tracked_set(inner)` -> set() (empty, not None); `validate_source_inventory({... ci_scripts:['scripts/tool.py'], file_digests:{correct sha256}}, inner)` -> AssertionError "S1 INVENTORY_UNTRACKED: sealed digests name paths git does not track (volatile host state): ['scripts/tool.py']". Polarity is fail-closed (loud false alarm, zero false-green risk) and the falsifier's prescribed path (fresh clone/worktree) is unaffected — but the rc2 lesson this guard encodes is precisely that a tamper detector false-alarming on legitimate verification trees erodes the integrity layer's credibility, and the error text ("volatile host state") would mislead that verifier. One-line hardening: trust ls-files only when `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` == root, else take the existing synthetic-tree notice path (validate_v6_assurance.py:196).
